patient_identity.statement: C1 is the distinct 15-year-old female in Table1 and case summary; family label, sex and last evaluation age match. Related C1/C2 and same-allele A1/E1 remain separate patients.

genotype.statement: C1 has the reported heterozygous TRAF3 variant NM_145725.3:c.339_340insTAGA, p.Q114X; coding notation, gene and heterozygosity agree. Packet hg38/NC_000014.9 genomic and VCF coordinates were not independently normalized against a reference.
limitations: Clinical sequence notation and zygosity supported; exact genome representation not independently verified.

segregation.statement: Q114X insertion found in C1 and affected father C2, absent from clinically well mother and two sisters; reported panel/exome investigation followed by Sanger. Paternal transmission is supported.

phase.statement: One heterozygous TRAF3 allele is reported; no biallelic cis/trans assertion is required or supported.

causal_confidence.statement: Authors attribute the immune dysregulation/immunodeficiency syndrome to monoallelic loss of TRAF3 expression, supported by multiple unrelated families, segregation/de novo evidence where available, and patient-cell studies. This supports the reported causal attribution but is not an independent modern clinical classification or verification of the packet’s exact OMIM subtype.
limitations: Small selected cohort, related participants and variable expressivity; cellular and common-variant association findings do not independently prove each case feature.
E1 has no family testing; functional assays are not individually demonstrated for every patient. Separate DataS1/checklist unavailable.

access_issues.detail: Supplementary Checklist/MDAR listed by PMC XML and supplementary cover, but unavailable. PMC web presented challenge; EuropePMC supplementaryFiles API returned not-open-access error; normal publisher supplementary-page request returnedHTTP403 challenge. University repository supplied MaterialsPDF only; search did not recover these files. No UI, bypass, credentials, contact or controlled-data access attempted.

Supplementary DataS1ZIP listed by PMC XML and supplementary cover, but unavailable. PMC web presented challenge; EuropePMC supplementaryFiles API returned not-open-access error; normal publisher supplementary-page request returnedHTTP403 challenge. University repository supplied MaterialsPDF only; search did not recover these files. No UI, bypass, credentials, contact or controlled-data access attempted.

limitations: Full paper completion remains false because the separate MDAR checklist and DataS1ZIP were not obtained/read; no absence claim.
No genotype reference remapping or new ACMG/OMIM clinical validation. All97phenotype entries and4alleles were individually compared; unchanged packet snapshots retain their hashes.

Case-specific narratives prevail over omission-based negatives; Table1UNK is unknown, not absent. Cohort-level expression and common-R118W associations do not prove every individual’s phenotype or malignant risk.
